agenda: Maintenance of peace and security of Ukraine
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to secure Council condemnation of the illegal referenda and attempted annexation, reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establish a clear non-recognition standard that isolates the Russian Federation. The main difficulty is holding a unified Council majority and resisting dilution by members seeking to avoid naming Russia, while the Russian Federation is expected to obstruct the text. We will work with co-sponsor the United States and like-minded members to keep the core operative demands intact.

messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the core message of the draft: the so-called referenda cannot be recognized and Ukraine's territorial integrity must be respected. However, Brazil cannot support a text that invokes Chapter VII and lacks any call for a ceasefire and renewed diplomacy. We therefore ask you to remove Chapter VII and add an operative paragraph urging an immediate cessation of hostilities and a negotiated peaceful settlement.
messages.China: China cannot support the current text as drafted. It is one-sided, invokes Chapter VII, and uses condemnatory language that will not help create conditions for dialogue. We ask the penholder to remove Chapter VII, replace the demand for withdrawal and the term “aggression” with a balanced call for cessation of hostilities and resumed negotiations, and add language on humanitarian access and political settlement. China will abstain if these concerns are not addressed.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution as circulated by Albania and the United States. It reflects France's position that the so-called referenda and any attempted annexation of Ukrainian territory are illegal and have no validity under international law. We urge the Council to proceed swiftly to a vote and call on all members to support the text.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the reaffirmation of Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and does not recognize any purported annexation. However, as drafted we would abstain: the text lacks an operative call for dialogue and peaceful settlement, and its Chapter VII invocation makes consensus harder. We request the addition of a clear call for negotiations and that the Chapter VII reference be replaced with Chapter VI language.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft as circulated. It reaffirms the fundamental principles of the Charter, including sovereignty, territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and it rightly rejects attempts to alter Ukraine’s borders by force. Ghana will vote in favour if the text is put to the Council.
messages.India: India thanks the penholder and remains deeply concerned by the situation in Ukraine. India’s consistent position is that disputes must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy while respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states. We will abstain on the current text and urge all parties to return to the path of peaceful negotiations.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports the thrust of the draft and commends the penholder for bringing forward this text. We ask for explicit references to international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access, as well as to accountability for violations of international law. These additions would strengthen the Council's response without altering the core demands. Ireland remains ready to support the text as amended.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the draft as circulated. We firmly reject the so-called referenda and attempted annexation and reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and call on the Russian Federation to immediately withdraw its forces. Kenya sees no need for changes at this stage and supports moving to a vote.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the draft as presented. It properly reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejects the attempted annexation and so-called referenda. We urge all Council members to vote in favour and call for the text's prompt adoption.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the draft as circulated and urges its swift adoption without amendment. The attempted annexation has no legal validity, and the Council must uphold Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We call on all members to vote in favour and on Russia to cease its aggression and withdraw its forces from Ukraine.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this unbalanced draft, which is based on unverified accusations and ignores the will of the people of Donbas, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia and the years of Ukrainian aggression. We request the deletion of all accusatory and Chapter VII elements and the inclusion of language on Ukraine's shelling of civilians and Western arms supplies. Otherwise, we will vote against the draft.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the draft as it stands. We believe the Council must be clear that the so-called referenda and attempted annexation have no legal validity and that Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity must be respected. We also urge all parties to pursue diplomatic channels and ensure humanitarian access, but we do not request amendments at this stage.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the draft resolution as circulated. Russia’s so-called referenda and attempted annexation of Ukrainian territory are illegal, have no validity under international law, and must not be recognized by any State. We urge the Council to send an unambiguous message in support of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and to proceed to a vote without weakening the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports revision 0 as co-sponsored. This text accurately condemns Russia's illegal so-called referenda and attempted annexation, demands withdrawal, and makes clear that any attempted annexation has no validity under international law. We should move promptly to a vote and maintain a unified Council position; Russia's veto cannot confer legitimacy on its actions.

steps.summary: The revision preserves the core Chapter VII condemnation and demands, while accepting Ireland's IHL and accountability additions and partially accommodating calls for humanitarian access and diplomacy. Brazil, China, Gabon, and India are expected to abstain; Russia is expected to vote against. Because a permanent member is expected to vote against, the text cannot be adopted despite likely majority support.

messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the draft's reaffirmation of sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-recognition of annexation, and its call for a cessation of hostilities and diplomacy. However, Brazil cannot support the invocation of Chapter VII, which risks escalation and is not conducive to a negotiated settlement. If Chapter VII remains, Brazil will abstain.
messages.China: China cannot support the current text because it retains Chapter VII and one-sided demands that will not help a peaceful settlement. We reiterate that PP9 must be deleted or replaced with a Chapter VI formulation, OP3 should call on all parties to cease hostilities and resume dialogue, and OP1 should be neutralized. If these core concerns are not reflected, China will abstain.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft as it stands and will vote in favour. The text clearly reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and rejects Russia’s attempted annexation as having no validity under international law. France urges all Council members to support this resolution without weakening its core provisions.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the addition of the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and diplomatic negotiations. However, Gabon cannot support a text that invokes Chapter VII, which risks deepening confrontation and prejudging enforcement action; we ask that it be replaced with Chapter VI. With that change, and with continued emphasis on peaceful settlement, sovereignty and territorial integrity, Gabon could support the draft.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft as it stands. It reflects our opposition to the attempted annexation and our commitment to Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a resumption of diplomatic dialogue consistent with the Charter. Ghana will vote in favour of the text.
messages.India: India remains deeply concerned at the escalation and reiterates the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States, cease hostilities, and return to dialogue and diplomacy. We cannot support a Chapter VII text that is unbalanced and prescriptive; our priority is a balanced call for peaceful settlement by all parties. Unless these changes are made, India will abstain. We also ask that the food and energy impact on developing countries be reflected.
messages.Ireland: Ireland welcomes the revisions that now capture international humanitarian law, unhindered humanitarian access and accountability. The draft clearly reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejects the attempted annexation. Ireland supports the text as it stands and urges the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the current draft as it stands. It reflects our principled position on sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-recognition of the acquisition of territory by force, while also calling for humanitarian protection and a negotiated settlement. We have no further changes and encourage the penholder to proceed to a vote.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the draft as it stands: it upholds the Charter, Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and rejects any attempted annexation. We value the inclusion of OP6 and OP8 on humanitarian access, cessation of hostilities and diplomacy, which are central to Mexico’s position. We urge the Council to speak with unity in support of this text.
messages.Norway: Norway strongly supports the draft as it stands. The attempted annexation has no legal validity under international law, and the Council should put this text to a vote without delay. Norway will vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: The current draft is unacceptable and cannot serve as a basis for consensus. It ignores the expressed will of the people of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia and prejudges the Russian Federation. We maintain our red lines: delete the accusatory paragraphs and Chapter VII, and reflect a balanced call for ceasefire, humanitarian access and an end to arms supplies to Ukraine. If this text is put to a vote in its present form, the Russian Federation will vote against it.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft as it stands. It clearly reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force, while also calling for humanitarian access and a peaceful settlement. We will vote in favour and encourage all Council members to do the same.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the revised draft as circulated. It clearly affirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, rejects Russia’s illegal attempted annexation, demands withdrawal of Russian forces, and underscores accountability. We have no further changes and urge the Council to proceed to a vote.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft as currently written and commends Albania for its leadership. The text clearly condemns Russia’s illegal referenda and attempted annexation, affirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and demands the immediate withdrawal of Russian forces. We see no need for changes and urge the Council to proceed to a vote without delay.

steps.summary: The revision preserves Chapter VII, Ukraine's territorial integrity, condemnation of the attempted annexation, and demands for withdrawal while adding India's food and energy security concern. Russia will vote against and veto the text; Brazil, China, Gabon, and India are expected to abstain. The draft retains ten affirmative votes.

reasons.Albania: Albania is the submitting delegation and strongly supports Ukraine’s territorial integrity, international law, and accountability for Russia’s aggression. It would speak and vote in favour to press the Council to condemn the illegal annexation attempts.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil’s negotiation red line was removal of Chapter VII, which was rejected; consistent with its stated position, Brazil abstains while still criticizing annexation and supporting territorial integrity and peaceful settlement.
reasons.China: China abstained on the 30 September 2022 UNSC draft because its red-line requests on Chapter VII and withdrawal language were rejected, while Beijing still avoids voting with Russia and emphasizes political settlement.
reasons.France: France strongly supports Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and consistently opposes Russia’s attempted annexations, so it would vote in favour and explain its position before the vote.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon had a red-line request to replace Chapter VII with Chapter VI, which was rejected; consistent with its actual position, it abstains while affirming opposition to annexation by force and support for peaceful settlement.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana’s stated position favoured support, and its foreign policy emphasizes sovereignty, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement, and humanitarian/developing-country concerns. Voting in favour is consistent with the actual Council alignment and Ghana’s last-round position.
reasons.India: India historically abstained on this September 2022 UNSC draft because its key red lines, especially deleting Chapter VII and modifying OP1/OP3, were rejected. Abstaining preserves India’s balanced position, support for territorial integrity and sovereignty, and call for dialogue without endorsing a Chapter VII condemnation of Russia.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland’s established position strongly supports Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejects unlawful annexation; the draft aligns with that policy, so Ireland votes in favour and explains its vote.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya’s established position strongly upholds the UN Charter, sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-recognition of forcible annexation, and its last-round position was support. Voting in favour with an explanation is consistent with Kenya’s record and interests.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico consistently upholds Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and opposes annexation by force, while favoring peaceful settlement and humanitarian principles; the draft aligns with that position and Mexico had already indicated support in negotiations.
reasons.Norway: Norway’s foreign policy strongly supports Ukraine’s territorial integrity and the Charter-based prohibition on annexation by force, so it would vote in favour. The statement reflects Norway’s likely explanation of vote before the Council and its alignment with like-minded Council members.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft condemns Russia’s actions and demands immediate withdrawal and rescission of annexation decisions under Chapter VII, crossing all Russian red lines. As a permanent member, Russia will vote against and thereby veto the resolution.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE’s last negotiation position was support, and its foreign policy emphasizes sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful settlement while urging de-escalation. In the actual Council vote on this draft, the UAE voted in favour.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom would support the draft because it affirms Ukraine’s territorial integrity, rejects Russia’s attempted annexations, and demands Russian withdrawal. The UK has no reason to abstain or oppose and would explain its vote before the vote to underline the illegitimacy of the referenda and annexation.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity while opposing Russia’s attempted annexation. It would therefore speak in favour and vote yes.

before.Albania: Albania votes in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. The so-called referenda and the announced annexation of Ukrainian territory are illegal, have no validity under international law, and cannot alter Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity or territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We call on the Russian Federation to immediately cease its aggression, withdraw all its military forces from Ukraine, rescind its unlawful decisions, and respect the Charter of the United Nations. The Security Council must uphold its responsibilities and send an unequivocal message that conquest by force will not be recognized.
before.Brazil: Brazil upholds the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine and does not recognize changes of borders by force. We also believe that the so-called referenda were not conducted in accordance with Ukrainian law or international standards and cannot serve as a basis for annexation. At the same time, Brazil has consistently opposed the invocation of Chapter VII in this context, which in our view risks deepening polarization and undermining the search for a negotiated, peaceful settlement. For that reason, Brazil will abstain on this draft resolution, while reiterating its call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and serious diplomacy aimed at a just and lasting peace.
before.China: Mr. President, China will abstain on this draft resolution. China’s position on the Ukraine issue is consistent and clear. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries should be respected, the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations should be upheld, and the legitimate security concerns of all countries should be taken seriously. The current draft retains condemnatory and withdrawal language and invokes Chapter VII, which is not conducive to de-escalation and does not take full account of the views of all Council members. China calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, cease hostilities, and resume dialogue and negotiations with a view to a political settlement. We therefore abstain.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The so-called referenda organized by Russia in the Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia regions have no legal value and cannot serve as a basis for any alteration of Ukraine’s status. By recognizing the independence of these regions and preparing their annexation, Russia is violating the United Nations Charter and the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. France firmly recalls that no acquisition of territory by force can be recognized. We demand that Russia immediately cease its aggression and withdraw all its military forces from Ukrainian territory, and we reaffirm the need for full respect for international humanitarian law and unimpeded humanitarian access.
before.Gabon: Gabon remains firmly attached to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We do not recognize any acquisition of territory by force, and we share the Council’s grave concern at the so-called referenda and attempted annexations. Gabon has consistently advocated that the Council should act in support of dialogue and peaceful settlement, and we regret that our proposal to base this text on Chapter VI rather than Chapter VII was not retained. For that reason, while reaffirming our support for international law, humanitarian access and negotiations, Gabon will abstain on the present draft.
before.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour of this draft resolution. Ghana has consistently upheld the principles of the Charter of the United Nations, including the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of all States within their internationally recognized borders. The so-called referenda and attempted annexation of Ukrainian territory cannot be accepted as a basis for altering borders by force. We support the draft’s demand for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to diplomacy and peaceful settlement. Ghana is also deeply concerned about the humanitarian consequences of this war and its impact on food and energy security, especially in developing countries. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and pursue dialogue in good faith.
before.India: India remains deeply concerned by the continuing conflict in Ukraine and its grave humanitarian consequences. Our position is clear and consistent: the global order must be anchored in the United Nations Charter, international law and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States. We have repeatedly called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to dialogue and diplomacy, since no durable solution can be achieved through confrontation or measures that deepen divisions. In view of our principled position and the text before the Council, India will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Ireland: Ireland will vote in favour of this resolution. We do so in defence of the Charter, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine, and the principle that territory shall not be acquired by force. The so-called referenda and attempted annexations are unlawful and have no validity. Ireland calls on the Russian Federation to cease its aggression, withdraw its forces, respect international humanitarian law, and engage in genuine diplomatic efforts for a peaceful settlement.
before.Kenya: Kenya votes in favour of this draft resolution. Kenya’s position is grounded in the United Nations Charter and in the African experience: territorial integrity cannot be altered by force, and the recognition of changes to borders by force cannot be accepted. The so-called referenda were not conducted in accordance with Ukrainian law or international standards and cannot serve as a basis for annexation. Kenya calls for respect for Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, for an immediate cessation of hostilities, for the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access, and for renewed diplomacy. Kenya also stresses the serious impact of this conflict on global food and energy security, particularly for developing countries.
before.Mexico: México votará a favor del proyecto de resolución. Nuestra posición se guía por los principios de la Carta de las Naciones Unidas: la soberanía, la independencia política, la integridad territorial de los Estados y el rechazo a la adquisición de territorio por la fuerza. Los llamados referendos realizados en partes de Ucrania no pueden servir de base para alterar fronteras internacionalmente reconocidas. México condena la anexión y reitera que ningún cambio de estatus territorial derivado del uso de la fuerza será reconocido. Al mismo tiempo, hacemos un llamado a la inmediata cesación de hostilidades, a la protección de la población civil, al acceso humanitario sin obstáculos y a la reanudación de una diplomacia seria orientada a una solución pacífica, conforme al derecho internacional.
before.Norway: Norway will vote in favour of this resolution. The so-called referenda and the attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia are unlawful and have no legitimacy under international law. Norway reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, and calls on the Russian Federation to immediately cease its aggression and withdraw its military forces from Ukraine. We also stress the need for full respect for international humanitarian law, safe humanitarian access, accountability, and a peaceful settlement consistent with the Charter of the United Nations.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation dissociates itself categorically from this draft resolution and will vote against it. The text submitted by Albania and co-sponsored by the United States is neither balanced nor aimed at a peaceful settlement. It is a one-sided, politically motivated attempt to impose an ultimatum on the Russian Federation while completely ignoring the years of suffering of the people of Donbas, the crimes committed by the Kyiv regime, and the legitimate right of the inhabitants of the Donetsk and Luhansk People’s Republics, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia to determine their own future. The draft selectively invokes the Charter, ignores the principle of equal and indivisible security, and makes demands that have no basis in reality. It also seeks to use Chapter VII as a mechanism of pressure against a permanent member of the Security Council. Such an approach is unacceptable and will only prolong the conflict and reduce the prospects for diplomacy. The Russian Federation will not support this text and votes against it.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Our position is grounded in the Charter’s fundamental principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. The UAE opposes the acquisition of territory by force and any unilateral act that risks deepening escalation. At the same time, we urge all parties to prioritize de-escalation, protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and return to meaningful diplomacy in pursuit of a just and sustainable peace consistent with international law.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. The so-called referenda organized by Russia in occupied parts of Ukraine have no legitimacy; they were conducted at gunpoint and cannot form the basis for any purported annexation. Russia’s attempts to annex Ukrainian territory are a grave violation of the UN Charter and international law. The United Kingdom calls on all members to uphold Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and to demand that Russia immediately withdraw its forces from Ukraine.
before.United States of America: The United States supports this resolution and urges all members to vote in favour. The so-called referenda were a sham, conducted at gunpoint and in violation of the Charter of the United Nations and Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The United States will never recognise Russia’s attempted annexation of Ukraine’s sovereign territory. We call on the Russian Federation to cease its aggression and withdraw its forces from Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders. This Council must uphold the Charter; a vote against this resolution is a vote against the principles on which this organisation was founded.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania regrets that the Security Council has once again been prevented from discharging its responsibility by a single veto—cast by the very permanent member whose aggression this resolution sought to address. The draft before us was not a radical text. It reaffirmed the Charter, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine, and the illegality of acquiring territory by force. It was supported by ten members and opposed by only one. That isolation speaks for itself.

A veto cannot legitimize illegal referenda or annexation. It cannot erase the borders of a sovereign State, and it cannot silence this Council forever. Albania will not accept that the last word belongs to force. We will continue to stand with Ukraine, to insist on full respect for the United Nations Charter, and to work with all responsible partners to ensure that the Russian Federation is held accountable for its aggression. The Security Council has failed today, but the principles of the Charter have not.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this resolution owing to the veto of the Russian Federation. This veto is not a sign of strength; it is a sign of isolation. The so-called referenda and the attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia have no legal value and cannot alter Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. France does not and will not recognize any acquisition of territory by force. We will continue to defend the Charter of the United Nations and to stand by Ukraine. We call on all States not to recognize any alteration of Ukraine’s status and to work for a peaceful settlement consistent with international law.
after.Ireland:
Mr President,

Ireland voted in favour of this resolution, and we deeply regret that the Security Council has been prevented from discharging its responsibility by the veto of the Russian Federation. The Russian Federation is the very party whose conduct is at issue. Its veto cannot confer legitimacy on the so-called referenda or on the attempted annexation of Ukrainian territory. Those acts are illegal under international law, have no validity, and must not be recognised by any Member State.

Ireland’s position is rooted in the Charter and in the principle that territory cannot be acquired by force. We reiterate our full support for Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. We call on the Russian Federation to cease its aggression, withdraw its forces from Ukraine, respect international humanitarian law and ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access.

The veto cannot silence this Council’s responsibility to uphold the Charter. Ireland will continue to work with partners, including in the General Assembly, to ensure that the position of the overwhelming majority of Member States is heard and that accountability is pursued.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has voted against this draft resolution and has used its legitimate right under the Charter of the United Nations to prevent the Security Council from being drawn into a one-sided and destructive course. The sponsors of this text did not seek a balanced decision or a peaceful settlement. They sought an ultimatum against the Russian Federation while ignoring the root causes of the crisis, including years of shelling of the people of Donbas and the refusal of Kyiv to implement the Minsk agreements.

The draft also ignored the free expression of will by the inhabitants of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia, and attempted to deny them the right to determine their own future. The Russian Federation rejects attempts to question these decisions and will continue to defend the legitimate rights and security of these people, as well as the national interests of our country.

We are not refusing serious diplomacy. We have repeatedly said that the Council must contribute to de-escalation and a political settlement, not to the legitimisation of the actions of the Kyiv regime and its Western patrons. A resolution based on slogans, dictates and Chapter VII cannot serve that purpose. The responsibility for the failure of this draft lies entirely with its sponsors.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President, the United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution because it upholds the Charter of the United Nations, the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine, and the principle that territory must not be acquired by force. Russia’s so-called referenda were a sham, conducted at gunpoint in occupied parts of Ukraine. They have no legitimacy, and Russia’s attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia has no validity under international law. 

We deeply regret that Russia has now used its veto to block this Council from discharging its responsibilities. A veto cannot legitimise an illegal annexation, and it cannot erase Ukraine’s internationally recognised borders. The United Kingdom will not recognise Russia’s purported annexation, nor any alteration of Ukraine’s status brought about by force. We call on Russia immediately to cease its aggression, withdraw all of its military forces from Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders, and rescind its unlawful decisions.

The United Kingdom reaffirms its steadfast support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We will continue to work with partners to uphold the Charter, ensure accountability for violations of international law, protect civilians, and support a just and lasting peace based on respect for Ukraine’s rights and territorial integrity.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States deeply regrets that this Council could not adopt a resolution that simply upheld the Charter of the United Nations. One permanent member—the very member responsible for this war and for the attempted annexation of Ukraine’s territory—has used its veto to shield itself. That veto does not change international law. It does not validate the sham referenda conducted at gunpoint. It does not make Russia’s attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia any less unlawful or any less null and void. The United States will never recognize Russia’s attempted annexation of Ukraine’s sovereign territory. We thank the members who voted in favour and reaffirmed the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. The United States will continue to stand with Ukraine and with all who defend the Charter. We will continue to support Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, to press for accountability for violations of international law, and to pursue a just and durable peace consistent with the Charter. Russia cannot veto the principles on which this Organization was founded. Thank you.
